einzeiler: Former UKY cheerleader pleads guilty in newborn's death and other crime updates.
kurzfassung: A former University of Kentucky athlete pleaded guilty to first-degree manslaughter in the death of her newborn son. In Pennsylvania, an incoming college freshman was murdered by her boyfriend with his mother's alleged help in the cover-up. Meanwhile, in Colorado, a husband's claim that his wife died by suicide collapsed after police found evidence pointing to murder.
stichpunkte: Lacyn Snelling changed her plea to guilty for first-degree manslaughter regarding her newborn son's death.
Court records showed Snelling deprived the infant of oxygen and hid the remains in a closet trash bag.
Caroline Heinz, an 18-year-old college freshman, was stabbed to death by her boyfriend Royce Moser in Pennsylvania.
Royce Moser's mother, Rachel Moser, allegedly helped clean the vehicle, dispose of the weapon, and wash bloody clothes.
In Colorado, Patrick Barnett claimed his wife Lindsay died by suicide in the shower.
Investigators doubted the suicide claim due to blood on the bedroom mattress and defensive scratches on Patrick's body.
Police uncovered Patrick's extramarital affair, and Lindsay's family refuted any claims of suicidal ideation.

clips.hook: Former athlete faces up to ten years in prison
clips.text: Former University of Kentucky athlete Laken Snelling admitted guilt in the death of her newborn son and faces up to a decade behind bars.

clips.hook: Plea deal for first degree manslaughter accepted
clips.text: Prosecutor Kimberly Baird outlined the manslaughter plea agreement accepted before Judge Diane Minifield after the defendant broke down in court.

beschreibung:
Former University of Kentucky cheerleader Laken Snelling enters a guilty plea after her newborn infant was discovered deceased in a trash bag inside a closet. In Pennsylvania, an incoming college soccer player is brutally stabbed to death by her boyfriend, whose mother allegedly helped clean the crime scene and conceal evidence. A Colorado husband faces first-degree murder charges after claiming his wife committed suicide, as investigators uncover defensive fingernail wounds and an undisclosed extramarital affair. Sydney Silvagni reports.
